name: Celtic No. 2 1897
designer: Unidentified in the consulted historical specimens
foundry: Farmer, as credited in the Government Printing Office document specimen
description: Light serif capitals and flowing figures from the twelve-point Celtic No. 2 cut, with gently bowed crossbars and a sweeping Q tail.
character_set_notes: Complete observed A–Z capitals, all ten figures, period and ampersand from the twelve-point cut. Space is a modern layout advance. Lowercase and unsupported punctuation are not encoded.
observed: All 26 capitals, ten figures and period are directly observed in the labelled twelve-point Celtic No. 2 cut. The 1897 GPO specimen supplies QUVWXYZ; the 1900 census specimen supplies A–P and all ten figures; the 1904 document specimen supplies RST and period, and explicitly attributes the cut to Farmer. Exact crops, comparisons and measurements accompany the sources. The assembled business card on job-room printed page39 (archive leaf55) supplies the ampersand; matching native letter construction and measured physical size identify the twelve-point setting.
reconstructed: No letter or figure forms are invented. Spacing, digital metrics, paper illumination correction and measured scan rotation are modern preparation choices.

revival.notes: One uniform scale and a measured rigid rotation per source row preserve historical proportions. No missing letterforms, synthetic lowercase or punctuation companions are supplied. Native comparisons include the matching job-room specimen; the retained source decisions distinguish sharper imagery from heavier printing. Historical source sizes are archived under source/specimen-cuts. The public family uses one coherent complete alphabet and figures; source size is provenance, not a separate font product.
